questions.question: You should check your motorcycle completely:
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Check your motorcycle completely before every ride.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear a tire going flat. A sudden change in how the bike handles is the usual sign of tire failure.

questions.question: As you slow or stop, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears with the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Provide you with an escape route.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should keep you out of blind spots, help you see and be seen, help you avoid hazards, help you avoid wind from other vehicles, and give you an escape route. Position yourself to discourage other drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: How can you increase your ability to be seen at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Ride close to vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: To be seen best at an intersection, ride with your headlight on and position yourself so oncoming traffic can see your motorcycle clearly. Keep a safe space cushion so you can take evasive action if needed. Do not assume eye contact with a driver means they see you.

questions.question: In a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider should lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider keeps their body upright.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: When braking, you should only use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time to stop. The brakes work best when used together.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions frequently to prevent boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives you the most space cushion.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives you the most space cushion.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly, so the safest lane position changes too. Choose the position that gives you the most space cushion and lets other drivers see you best.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles. These crashes happen just a few minutes after the rider starts riding.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat, the rider can often hear it.
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire go flat. Instead, you may notice the motorcycle's handling suddenly changes.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip the handlebars tight and speed up to get past the hazard.
Ride on the shoulder instead of on the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to escape the wobble.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—this makes the motorcycle more unstable. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slow down by gradually closing the throttle, shift your weight forward and down, and move to the side of the road. Avoid using the brakes, as they can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Maximum straight-line braking is done by:

options.text: Using both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel.
Using both the front and rear brakes while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: To stop in the shortest distance on a straight road, use both brakes. Avoid locking either brake.
